subject: physics
question_text: State Avogadro's hypothesis and show that it follows from the kinetic theory of gases.

verification.note: Sourced from the Sri Chaitanya IPE Study Material for Jr. Students 2026-27 edition, physics volume, Chapter 13 Very Short Answer Question 2 (printed p.136). Only the question was taken; the answer, its steps and its mark split are original work — see docs/ORIGINALITY_MATHS.md. The 1 + 1 mark split is INVENTED and is a CLAIM until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it. Physics hand-checked: Avogadro's hypothesis (equal volumes of gases at the same temperature and pressure hold equal numbers of molecules) follows from PV = ⅔N(½mv̄²) because ½mv̄² depends on temperature alone, so equal P, V and T force equal N for every gas — matching NCERT Class-11 Chapter 13.

recall_prompt: Say the steps you would write for this answer, in order. You can speak in English, in Telugu, or in both.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: The hypothesis
lines: of gases at the same temperature and
steps.margin_note: First mark. The words equal volumes, same temperature and same pressure must all appear.
steps.why: Equal numbers of molecules is what makes the mole the same size for every gas — one mole always holds the Avogadro number of particles, whatever the gas.
common_mistakes: Saying equal volumes of gases have equal mass. The hypothesis is about the number of molecules, not the mass.
Leaving out same temperature and same pressure — the hypothesis holds only under those conditions.

recall.must_convey: That equal volumes of gases at the same temperature and pressure contain equal numbers of molecules.
accept: equal volumes have equal numbers of molecules
reject: PV equals two thirds N half m v squared

steps.memory_tip: Same volume, same temperature, same pressure — the same number of molecules inside.

steps.label: Kinetic theory justification
lines: At the same temperature ½mv̄² is the
same for every gas. So equal P and V
force equal N for every gas.
steps.margin_note: Second mark. Start from PV = ⅔N(½mv̄²) and state that ½mv̄² is fixed by temperature alone.
steps.why: The average translational kinetic energy of a molecule depends only on the absolute temperature, so at the same temperature every gas has the same ½mv̄². Equal P and V then force N to be equal too, whatever the gas.
common_mistakes: Thinking the result depends on the type of gas. ½mv̄² is the same for every gas at a given temperature, whatever the molecular mass.
Forgetting to state that P and V must both be equal before N can be forced equal.

recall.must_convey: That PV equals two thirds N half m v bar squared, and since half m v bar squared is fixed by temperature, equal P and V force equal N.
accept: PV equals two thirds N half m v squared
same temperature gives same kinetic energy
equal P and V force equal N
reject: equal volumes have equal numbers of molecules
heard_as: two thirds N half m v squared

steps.memory_tip: Same T fixes the energy per molecule. Same P and V then force the same N.

insider_note: The hypothesis alone is one mark — the second needs PV = ⅔N(½mv̄²) written out and connected to equal N.
